Reviewed against the base and the KVM tap naming. This is a clean fix and CI backs it (the dualtor KVM Elastictest run passed). The logic is correct and the physical path is preserved.

What I verified
- The KVM-first match is right. On KVM, sonic.xml.j2 names the data-port taps <dut_name>-<n> (ansible/roles/vm_set/templates/sonic.xml.j2:99,111), and self.duthost.hostname == dut_name, so picking the bridge port that startswith "<hostname>-" targets exactly that ToR without the "upper ToR has the smaller vlan suffix" ordering assumption.
- The physical path is not regressed. Physical bridge ports are server-NIC subinterfaces (<port>.<vlan>) that do not start with the DUT hostname, so they fall through the for-else to the original filter-by-"."/sort/zip logic, which is preserved unchanged.
- Fail-loud is preserved: if the bridge has no port for this hostname, the fallback filter yields nothing and it raises ValueError, now with bridge_ports included, which is a nice debugging improvement.

One small, non-blocking note
- startswith("<hostname>-") assumes no DUT hostname is a dash-prefix of another on the same bridge (e.g., "vlab-01" vs "vlab-01-b"). I checked this closely and it is not a real concern today: the baa-* bridge carries exactly one data port per ToR (vm_topology.py create_dualtor_cable attaches only iaa/upper/lower/nic), the mgmt tap <dut_name>-0 is stripped before front-panel mapping (kvm_port.py) so it never lands on the baa bridge, and the real dualtor pairs (vlab-05/06, vlab-11/12, vlab-vpp-03/04, vlab-vpp-05/06, dtor3-dut0/dut1) are never dash-prefixes of each other. If you ever expect a hostname that is a prefix of another, collecting the matches and asserting exactly one (or an exact "<hostname>-<port>" shape check) would make it fail loud instead of silently steering to the sibling ToR. Optional.

Looks good to me. Since this is the enablement helper for the dualtor-aa-vpp cases onboarded in #27663, worth landing them together (or this one first) so the onboarded tests actually pass on the AA VPP testbed.

Auto-generated lossless BUFFER_PG coverage.

The patch deliberately does not carry  BUFFER_PG|<port>|3-4 .  buffermgrd  derives those on link-up from PORT  speed  plus  CABLE_LENGTH , because the profile name is parameterised —  pg_lossless_<speed>_<cable>_profile  — and PFC headroom scales with link speed and cable round-trip time. That is why  BUFFER_QUEUE|<port>|3-4  is pushed while  BUFFER_PG|<port>|3-4  is not: egress profiles are fixed names, the ingress lossless one has to be computed. The platform team confirmed this behaviour, and the NDM production patch we diff against contains no such op.
